entry.name: Seed-Start Grant SA
entry.summary: Matched grants for early-stage South Australian businesses commercialising an innovative product or service.
entry.eligibility: Australian-incorporated company with an active ABN; non-tax-exempt and GST-registered; turnover below A$1 million in each of the prior three financial years; based, or willing to be based, in South Australia before the project starts.
entry.limits: Seed grants are A$50,000–A$100,000 at a 2:1 government-to-applicant match. Start grants are A$100,001–A$500,000 at a 1:1 match. Defined commercialisation projects and a unique product or sustainable competitive advantage are required; confirm current round terms.

facts.Geography: Based, or willing to be based, in South Australia

provenance.evidence: The official business.gov.au programme page lists the grant as open, publishes both matched-funding bands and match ratios, and requires an Australian company with ABN and GST registration, turnover below A$1 million in each of the prior three financial years, and a South Australian base or commitment to relocate before project commencement.

entry.name: First Nations Innovation Acceleration Program QLD
entry.value: Investment grants up to A$100,000 plus advisory services
entry.summary: Funding and dedicated business advisory support for established Queensland First Nations businesses developing innovative products or services.
entry.eligibility: A First Nations-owned business that is established and operating in Queensland, developing an innovative product or service, and seeking advisory support and possible funding to accelerate that innovation.
entry.limits: Applications close 4 February 2027, or earlier if fully subscribed. The source describes support for mature, established businesses, so this is a scale-up pathway rather than an idea-stage startup grant.

facts.Eligibility: First Nations-owned, established and operating in Queensland
facts.Closing date: 4 February 2027; may close earlier if fully subscribed

provenance.evidence: The official business.gov.au listing shows the programme open to 4 February 2027, subject to earlier closure if fully subscribed, and specifies Queensland operation, First Nations ownership, an innovative product or service, grants up to A$100,000, and targeted advisory support for mature businesses.

entry.name: Regional Artificial Intelligence Initiative — British Columbia
entry.summary: Federal project funding for qualifying B.C. businesses commercialising AI or integrating AI into operations.
entry.eligibility: Incorporated business operating in British Columbia: commercialization projects require at least 1 year of operation and 1–500 FTE; AI adoption projects require at least 3 years and 5–500 FTE.
entry.limits: Applications close 23 November 2026 at 12:00 pm Pacific. Interest-free repayable contribution covers up to 50% of eligible project costs; at least 50% of project funding must be confirmed from non-government sources. Routine off-the-shelf AI purchases are excluded. Repayment typically starts one year after project completion and runs monthly for five years.

facts.Funding: Repayable; up to 50% of eligible costs

provenance.evidence: PacifiCan states this business intake is open through 12:00 pm Pacific on 23 November 2026. Incorporated B.C. businesses can seek C$200,000–C$5 million in interest-free repayable project contributions covering up to 50% of eligible costs. The who-can-apply and funding pages specify project-specific operating history and employee thresholds, at least 50% confirmed non-government co-funding, and repayment and cost restrictions.

entry.name: START — West of England
entry.org: TechSpark and West of England Mayoral Combined Authority
entry.value: Free 28-hour programme; possible funded incubator placement
entry.summary: Training, workshops and mentoring for people developing an early-stage technology business in the West of England.
entry.eligibility: Applicants must be over 18 and live in Bristol, South Gloucestershire or Bath and North East Somerset. For people with an idea, not yet trading, or within the first year of operating.
entry.limits: No new cohort dates are confirmed. The operator invites expressions of interest for future cohorts. A six-month funded incubator place is a possible outcome after pitching, not a guaranteed programme benefit.
entry.status: Future cohort dates unconfirmed; expressions of interest open

facts.Programme: 28 hours of learning, workshops and mentoring
facts.Location: Bristol, South Gloucestershire, or Bath and North East Somerset
facts.Next cohort: Dates not confirmed; expression of interest

provenance.evidence: TechSpark describes START as a free 28-hour early-stage technology founder programme for residents of Bristol, South Gloucestershire, or Bath and North East Somerset; it says future dates are not yet confirmed and offers an expression of interest. GOV.UK independently lists the programme for early-stage or first-year businesses in the West of England and describes the training, workshops, mentoring and opportunity to pitch for an incubator place.
